name: Joah
overview: Joah was a male figure known primarily for his role as Hezekiah's recorder, a position of responsibility during King Hezekiah's reign. Scripture does not specify his tribe or additional background details, focusing instead on his official capacity in the royal administration.
namesAndTitles: The name Joah means 'y-h-v-h is brother,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges the Lord (Yahweh). This proper name is recorded in 2 Kings 18:18 and does not indicate it was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Joah was the son of Asaph, as explicitly stated in 2 Kings 18:18. Beyond this father-son relationship, Scripture does not provide further family details for Joah.
scriptureSignificance: Joah's significance lies in his administrative role as Hezekiah's recorder, which would have involved documenting official matters and possibly acting as a royal secretary or chronicler. His position underscores the organized governance under Hezekiah's reign and highlights the importance of faithful record-keeping in the biblical narrative.
